mainEntity.name: How much does it cost to replace a Mercedes G Class G 55 AMG engine in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Mercedes G Class G 55 AMG engine replacement typically costs between £5,500 and £9,000 depending on condition type and whether fitting is included. M113K supercharged V8 units range from £5,500 to £9,000 supply only. Rebuilt M113K (G 55 AMG): £5,500-£9,000 supply only. Reconditioned units: £4,500-£7,000. Used engines from breakers: £2,500-£4,800 but higher risk. Labour for supply & fit adds £800-£1,500 to any engine price.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of M113K supercharger failure in a G 55 AMG?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M113K's supercharger system has several warning signs before complete failure. Loss of power or reduced boost pressure. Whining or grinding noise from the supercharger. Supercharger clutch not engaging (no boost under acceleration). Belt slippage or unusual belt noise.

mainEntity.name: Is the M113K engine in the G 55 AMG reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M113K is considered one of the most robust German performance engines. However, the supercharger system requires attention at higher mileages. Supercharger clutch and bearings are the main weak points. Oil leaks from valve cover gaskets are common. The engine block and internals are exceptionally durable. With preventative maintenance, 150,000+ miles is realistic.

mainEntity.name: Should I repair or replace my G 55 AMG engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Repair if the failure is isolated (e.g., supercharger clutch, valve cover gaskets, transmission valve body). Replace if there's bottom end damage, bore scoring, or catastrophic supercharger failure that has sent debris through the engine. Supercharger clutch replacement: £700-£1,100 - excellent value if caught early. Valve cover gasket replacement: £350-£550 - good preventative maintenance. Full M113K rebuild: £5,500-£9,000 - for catastrophic failure or 150k+ miles. Given G 55 AMG values (£15,000-£45,000), a rebuilt engine is typically good value.

mainEntity.name: How do I know which engine code my G 55 AMG has?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check your vehicle log book (V5C) for the engine number, which includes the engine code prefix. V5C log book shows full engine number with code prefix. Engine code stamped on cylinder block (visible from under vehicle). G 55 AMG (2004-2006): M113.982 (476hp). G 55 AMG (2006-2012): M113.993 (500hp). Service history documents list engine type.

mainEntity.name: Can I fit a used G 55 AMG engine myself?

acceptedAnswer.text: We strongly advise against DIY fitting on a G 55 AMG. The complex 4MATIC system, supercharger plumbing, gearbox alignment, and ECU coding requirements demand specialist equipment and expertise. 4MATIC transfer case alignment requires specialist knowledge. Supercharger system requires precise reassembly. ECU coding and immobiliser synchronisation needed. Specialist supply & fit costs £800-£1,500 - worth every penny.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz G Class G 55 AMG - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Mercedes Benz G 55 AMG represented the first factory-built AMG G-Class, transforming the boxy off-roader into a supercharged V8 performance icon. Powered by the M113K Kompressor engine, it defined AMG's G-Class lineage from 2004 to 2012.

milestones.description: G 55 AMG Kompressor launched as standard catalogue model, M113K 5.4L supercharged V8, 476hp (350kW), 5-speed 722.6 automatic
Power output increased to 500hp (373kW), torque 700Nm, improved supercharger calibration
Facelift with revised styling, continued 500hp output
G 55 AMG replaced by G 63 AMG with M157 twin-turbo V8, ending the supercharged V8 era

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz G Class G 55 AMG Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mercedes Benz G Class G 55 AMG relies on the M113K supercharged V8 - a fundamentally robust engine that has developed a well-documented reputation for specific, predictable failures. The supercharger clutch is the most common failure point driving replacement demand, while oil leaks and supercharger bearing wear also feature prominently. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty. Below we break down the most common G 55 AMG engine failures, what they cost to fix, and when replacement is the smarter financial decision.

problems.h4: M113K Supercharger Clutch Failure - Why the G 55 AMG Loses Boost and Power
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Benz G Class G 55 AMG (M113.982, M113.993, 2004-2012)
problems.rootCause: The electromagnetic clutch that engages and disengages the supercharger can fail, leading to a loss of boost pressure and reduced engine performance. The supercharger bearings also wear out over time, causing a whining noise and eventual failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace electromagnetic clutch assembly, inspect belt and tensioner
repairOptions.longevity: 50k-80k miles; excellent value if caught early

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full supercharger strip-down, new bearings, clutch, seals, and pulley
repairOptions.longevity: 80k-120k miles; recommended if whining noise present

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M113K with rebuilt supercharger, upgraded components
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty; required for catastrophic failure

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical G 55 AMG is worth £15,000-£45,000 depending on condition and mileage【INDUSTRY ESTIMATE】. The full replacement cost of £5,500-£9,000 is modest relative to vehicle value for most examples, making a specialist rebuilt engine excellent value for preservation. For vehicles worth under £12,000, evaluate repair options first.
problems.recommendation: At the first sign of power loss or abnormal whining from the supercharger, have the clutch and bearings inspected. The specialist clutch replacement at £700-£1,100 is excellent value if caught early. If the supercharger has been whining for some time, budget for the full rebuild route - ignoring bearing wear risks catastrophic supercharger failure that can send debris through the engine.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M113K Mercedes Benz G Class G 55 AMG engine prices

problems.h4: M113K Oil Leaks - Why the G 55 AMG Drips Oil
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Benz G Class G 55 AMG (M113.982, M113.993, 2004-2012)
problems.rootCause: The M113K engine is prone to oil leaks from valve cover gaskets that harden and crack over time, oil cooler seal degradation, and front crankshaft seal leaks that can contaminate the serpentine belt.

repairOptions.tier: Minor - Valve Cover Gasket Replacement (Both Sides)
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace valve cover gaskets, breather cover seals, new spark plug tube seals
Replace valve cover gaskets, oil cooler seals, front crankshaft seal, PCV system
repairOptions.longevity: 80k+ miles; recommended if multiple leaks present

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M113K with new gaskets, seals, and upgraded components
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty; for catastrophic failure

problems.vehicleValueCheck: On a G 55 AMG worth £15,000-£45,000, the valve cover gasket replacement at £350-£550 is excellent value. Full engine replacement is only justified for catastrophic failure or extremely high-mileage examples.
problems.recommendation: Oil leaks on the M113K are rarely urgent but should not be ignored - oil dripping onto the exhaust manifolds can create smoke and, in extreme cases, fire risk. The specialist valve cover gasket replacement at £350-£550 is cost-effective and should last 80k+ miles. If you're already addressing one leak, consider doing the full top-end reseal - the labour overlaps significantly.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M113K Mercedes Benz G Class G 55 AMG engine prices

problems.h4: 722.6 Transmission Valve Body Issues - Why the G 55 AMG Shifts Harshly
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Benz G Class G 55 AMG (M113.982, M113.993, 2004-2012)
problems.rootCause: The 5-speed 722.6 automatic transmission's valve body and conductor plate can develop wear, causing delayed gear shifts, harsh shifting, and solenoid failure. The torque converter can also fail, leading to shuddering and slipping.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace conductor plate, valve body solenoids, transmission fluid and filter
Replace torque converter, valve body, conductor plate, full transmission service
repairOptions.longevity: 120k+ miles; if torque converter shudder present

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M113K and rebuilt 722.6 transmission

problems.vehicleValueCheck: On a G 55 AMG worth £15,000-£45,000, the valve body service at £500-£800 is a sensible investment. The combined engine and transmission replacement is only justified for catastrophic failure.
problems.recommendation: The 722.6 transmission is generally reliable but benefits from regular fluid changes every 60,000 miles. At the first sign of harsh shifting or delayed engagement, have the valve body inspected - the specialist conductor plate and solenoid replacement at £500-£800 is far cheaper than a full transmission rebuild. Don't ignore torque converter shudder; it can cause debris that damages the entire transmission.
